passage: In the group room at the library in Uppsala, Ingrid had already typed the whole outline and given out the sections in her own order. "This is fine, right?" she said, not waiting. Astrid's jaw tightened. In earlier meetings she had nodded and gone quiet to avoid a quarrel, and her ideas had never made it in. This time she opened the shared document. "I looked at the marking guide. Section three needs a comparison, and I can write it. Let's put who does which part in the document, with dates, so everyone can see." Ingrid paused, then typed Astrid's name next to section three. "Okay. Add the dates."

qa.q: Where did Ingrid and Astrid meet to work?
qa.a: They met in the group room at the library in Uppsala.

qa.q: Why had Astrid gone quiet in earlier meetings?
qa.a: Astrid wanted to avoid a quarrel, so she nodded and stayed silent, though her ideas never made it in.

qa.q: What worked in how Astrid spoke up this time?
qa.a: She pointed to the marking guide and asked for the tasks and dates in the shared document, using facts and writing instead of an argument. 🙂

qa.q: How might Ingrid see Astrid's request?
qa.a: Ingrid paused, then agreed, which suggests she may not have noticed how much she had decided alone.

grounding: One member controls everything; the other speaks with facts and gets tasks shared in writing.

Nirmala: i've rewritten everyone's slides. final version attached. please don't change anything
Lokesh: hey nirmala, thanks for the effort
Lokesh: but my section now has figures i didn't use, and two of them are from 2015
Lokesh: can we split it in writing? who owns which slides, and changes go through the owner
Nirmala: i just want it to be perfect 😅
Lokesh: me too. i've redone my slides with the 2023 data, source link here
Ritika: agree with lokesh. i'll take slides 8 to 10
Nirmala: ok. fair. i'll do intro and conclusion only
Lokesh: great, i'll make a table in the doc with names and slides
Nirmala: sorry. i get controlling when i'm stressed
Lokesh: we all do. deadline's friday, we've got this 👍

qa.q: How old were two of the figures in Lokesh's section?
How does Lokesh seem to feel about the rewrite, and how does it show?
qa.a: Frustrated but calm: Lokesh thanks Nirmala first, then answers with facts instead of anger.

qa.q: How did Lokesh push back instead of staying silent?
qa.a: By pointing out specific problems (unused figures, 2015 data), redoing the slides with 2023 data and a source, and proposing slide ownership in writing.

qa.q: How does Nirmala see the situation once challenged?
qa.a: Nirmala admits to getting controlling when stressed and takes only the intro and conclusion.

grounding: Shows one groupmate controlling everything, and responding with facts and a written split of tasks rather than silence.

passage:
For their NSS water survey in Kolar district, Hemant had taken charge of everything: which wells to visit, who asked what, even who carried the clipboard. At the gram panchayat office he answered every question himself while Farida and two others stood behind him.
On the walk back past the paddy fields, Farida's stomach churned. Staying quiet was easier. But she had grown up in a village like this one and knew the women came to the handpump at 6 a.m., not at noon, when Hemant had scheduled the visits.
That evening she said, "Hemant, the noon visits are missing most of the women. In my aunt's village it's the same; they fetch water at dawn. Can we switch?"
He frowned. "I've already planned it."
"I know. Can we write down who leads which village? I'll take the dawn visits in two villages." She had already drawn up the table.
The others nodded. Hemant looked at the paper, then agreed, a little stiffly. At dawn on Friday, Farida's clipboard filled up within an hour.

qa.q: At what time had Hemant scheduled the visits?
What was Farida feeling on the walk back?
qa.a: Uneasy, with her stomach churning, and tempted to stay quiet because it was easier.

qa.q: How did Farida challenge Hemant's control?
qa.a: With a fact from her own experience (women fetch water at dawn), a written table of who leads which village, and an offer to take the dawn visits.
He frowned and said he had already planned it, then agreed a little stiffly once he saw the table.

grounding: Illustrates a dominating groupmate, and speaking up with facts and a written split of tasks instead of staying silent.
